live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: a transport verb at Ezek.47.1 (“He brought me back to the door of the temple” (web:Ezek.47.1)) continues the vision after the hard seam at 46.24/47.1; a second transport verb follows immediately at 47.2, then the measuring sequence proper (3-5, four successive measured wadings) -- disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation from a pure vision_report, since the passage briefly carries temple_measurement's own device before returning to vision narrative. The row covers the river's rise from the threshold (1-2), the four measured wadings (3-5), the 'have you seen, son of man' address (6) and the return to the bank, the riverside trees and the healed sea (7-10), the unhealed swamps (11, a K/Q verse), and the closing description of the riverbank trees bearing monthly fruit (12), where the construction glossed 'its months' is disclosed as the book's final chodesh-root homograph, not a date formula. Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.47.12 ends the row; the next verse, 47.13, opens with a fresh messenger formula addressed to the land-division topic -- a genre shift from vision to statute/allotment, the hard seam at 47.12/47.13.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 47.5/47.6 to isolate the measuring circuit (47.3-5) as its own temple_measurement row. It is weighed and held on stated grounds. The rival's near face, Ezek.47.6, IS licensed: the verse is both a said-to-me verse and a guided-motion verse (וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי, וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי), and it is a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses), so a seam there would not be device-free. Its far face, Ezek.47.5, carries the fourth measure-verb occurrence and a content close (נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יֵעָבֵֽר), with no close-role formula and no parashah mark, so the rival is one-faced rather than two-faced. The row holds against it on three stated grounds: Ezek.47.6's question looks BACK at the measuring just reported and its motion returns the prophet to the bank inside one scene rather than opening a new one; 47:1-12 reads as a single region with 47:6 inside it as interior texture; and the only further signal at 47:6 is the WEB's mid-verse paragraph, which is tier-4 and never corroborates a seam. Guided-motion verbs stand inside the measuring circuit, though not at its head: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, Ezek.47.3 does not BEGIN with a guided-motion verb (it opens בְּצֵאת הָאִ֥ישׁ) but does carry וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי later in the verse, and Ezek.47.4 carries that same form twice. Both verses are members of the same counted class, standing inside the measuring circuit, weighed and not taken, since each of those verbs steps the prophet one wading further after a measuring of a thousand cubits rather than opening a new scene. The measuring sequence therefore remains texture inside the single river vision running 47.1-12, disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation rather than split into a separate row (oshb:Ezek.47.5, oshb:Ezek.47.3, oshb:Ezek.47.6).
live_prose.device_notes: Category deviation, disclosed: this row's span briefly carries temple_measurement's own device (the four measured wadings, 47.3-5) inside an otherwise vision_report unit; disclosed in this one sentence rather than split into a separate row, since no formula bounds 47.3-5 off on either side. The two transport verses inside that circuit were weighed as rival onsets and not taken. A seam at 47.2/47.3 would strand 47.1-2 as a two-verse row, and a row that short is held only for a complete word-event unit, which those two verses are not; a seam at 47.3/47.4 would part the second measuring of a thousand from the one before it. K/Q notes fall at Ezek.47.8, 47.10, 47.11 and 47.12 inside this row -- a locally dense cluster -- disclosed as textual-variant sites; no boundary is argued from any of them. Ezek.47.12 carries the construction glossed 'its months', the last of the book's chodesh-root homographs, disclosed as NOT a date formula.
